lead: Michigan plumbing deals with cold winters, basements, old housing and lead service lines. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Detroit to the Upper Peninsula.
risk: lead service lines, flooded basements and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, flooded basements and frozen pipes
why: Michigan requires water utilities to replace lead service lines, a rule shaped by the Flint water crisis. Older homes in Detroit, Grand Rapids and Flint also have galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains.

Heavy rain floods basements and backs up sewers, as in the 2021 Detroit-area floods. Winters freeze pipes, especially in the Upper Peninsula. Michigan licenses plumbers through LARA's Bureau of Construction Codes.
tips: Ask your utility about your service line.
Test your sump pump and add a battery backup.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
areas: Calls come from Detroit and its suburbs, Grand Rapids, Lansing, Ann Arbor, Flint, Kalamazoo, Traverse City and the Upper Peninsula.

faq.q: Is Michigan replacing lead water lines?
faq.a: Yes. Michigan requires water utilities to replace lead service lines over time. Ask your utility about your address, and a plumber can check the pipe where it enters your home.
